source.extraction: First HTML pre block; remove HTML tags, HTML-unescape once, UTF-8 encode; preserve leading and trailing whitespace.

patches.reason: Make read errors signed and distinct from EOF, retry interrupted reads/writes and complete partial writes, check allocation failures, index the complement table with unsigned bytes, and stop before forming the upstream before-base cursor. These changes preserve output for valid FASTA input.

differences: C rewrites each record in place with pointers and inserts line breaks before reversing; YIAN receives record/header/sequence offsets into an owned u8 slice, walks sequence bytes backward, complements them and emits new 60-byte lines through a buffered writer.
Both retain headers, record order and the same IUPAC complement mapping; YIAN never forms a pointer before the input allocation.
C reads with read/realloc into a contiguous buffer; YIAN reads stdin in 8192-byte chunks and extends a Vec<u8>, preserving all input bytes before processing records.
C locates records backward through raw pointers; YIAN scans record headers forward and passes validated u64 offsets to process.
Both emit the full reverse-complement FASTA and return status 0 for the official input.
